text.deployment: The Succession Wars variant represents the inevitable simplification of the Prowler under the industrial and technological pressures of that era. The advanced automation suite is stripped in favor of a conventional multi-crew arrangement, and the cargo bay is reconfigured as a dedicated infantry compartment, giving the vehicle more direct combat utility. The long-range missile rack receives an ammunition upgrade to provide better fire support to the infantry it carries. Multiple manufacturers across the Inner Sphere and Periphery produce this variant, making it the most widely encountered Prowler configuration. Its low production cost and minimal maintenance requirements ensure continued manufacture even in resource-limited facilities.

A field modification developed during the Succession Wars, the Support variant adapts the standard Prowler chassis for rear-echelon utility roles. Armament is simplified to reduce crew workload and maintenance demands, while additional cargo capacity is freed for supplies and spare parts. Performed by unit technicians rather than dedicated conversion facilities, the Support variant shows considerable variation between individual vehicles. It fills a gap between dedicated logistics transports and combat carriers in second-line and garrison formations that lack the budget for purpose-built support vehicles.

The PAT-001 entered service in 2650 as the first production run of the Puma, with weapons matching the later PAT-005 standard but persistent environmental control failures that made extended combat operations dangerous for crews. Internal temperatures frequently exceeded safe operating limits during sustained engagements, and the design was withdrawn from front-line service once the more reliable PAT-005 became available. The PAT-001 served primarily in garrison and militia roles within the Star League, where its firepower remained useful even as its design flaws limited its broader deployment. Numbers declined rapidly through the Succession Wars as vehicles were lost and no production continued.

Introduced in 2657, the PAT-002 addressed some of the PAT-001's environmental control problems but introduced new ammunition handling failures that made the design equally hazardous in prolonged engagements. Missile misfeeds and breech malfunctions reduced effective firepower at critical moments, compounding the difficulties crews already faced. Like its predecessor, the PAT-002 was deployed primarily in Star League garrison roles rather than the assault function it was designed for. As the PAT-005 entered production, surviving PAT-002 vehicles were generally reassigned to secondary theaters or training units before disappearing entirely during the Succession Wars.

The PAT-005 is the definitive production variant of the Puma, resolving the critical flaws of its predecessors and entering service with the SLDF in 2681. Deployed in armored assault and fire-support formations, it served with Regular Armored Command units across the Star League and saw action through the final decades of the Star League era. ComStar maintained production at Pandora 'Mech Works on Terra following the Coup, keeping the design available to the Com Guards throughout the Succession Wars. Odin Manufacturing on Orestes produced the PAT-005 for the Free Rasalhague Republic's defensive formations during the late thirty-first century. The Word of Blake also fielded large numbers of the PAT-005 as the backbone of Protectorate Militia armored elements after restarting production in 3065. The PAT-005 remains the most widely recognized and most commonly encountered variant of the Puma.

The PAT-005b, designated the Royal variant, was developed in 2751 for the SLDF's Royal Divisions and served exclusively with those elite formations. The XL power plant frees sufficient weight to accommodate an extended-range particle cannon, twin Streak missile launchers replacing the original SRM rack, Artemis IV guidance on the LRM launchers, and a pulse laser at the rear. CASE protects the ammunition storage throughout the hull. Production at Pandora 'Mech Works halted with the factory's destruction or mothballing following the Amaris Coup and was not restored during the Succession Wars. After the Jihad, the production line was brought back online at the same facility to replace the PAT-007 in Republic of the Sphere service, with the design finding a new role as a capable assault vehicle for post-Jihad forces requiring proven Star League-era technology.

The PAT-007 entered production in 3069 at Pandora 'Mech Works as the standard combat vehicle for the Word of Blake Protectorate Militia. Designed to equip militia formations rather than elite units, it exchanges the original PPC and separate missile systems for a heavy particle cannon and three multi-missile launchers capable of engaging targets at both short and long range. The heavy ferro-fibrous armor and CASE provide significantly better crew protection than the original PAT-005. Machine gun arrays and a B-Pod give the tank meaningful capability in urban environments against infantry and battle armor. The C3i computer ties PAT-007 units into Blakist Level II formations, sharing targeting data across the formation and multiplying the effectiveness of coordinated fire missions. Odin Manufacturing on Orestes also produced the PAT-007 for Free Rasalhague Republic and later Clan Ghost Bear forces during the Civil War. Post-Jihad production on Terra was discontinued due to the C3i system's incompatibility with Republic of the Sphere doctrine.

The PAT-008 is a rare command variant produced in 3069 for senior Word of Blake Protectorate officers who required both survivability and direct combat capability in the field. An extended-range particle cannon linked to a dedicated targeting computer provides highly accurate long-range fire, backed by three Artemis-guided multi-missile launchers for sustained saturation fire. Six anti-missile systems and three B-Pods ring the hull to counter missiles and battle armor threats, while a Guardian ECM suite denies electronic support to nearby enemies. Heavy ferro-fibrous armor matches the protection level of the PAT-007. Produced in limited numbers and deployed exclusively to high-value command elements, the PAT-008 was rarely found in standard line formations. Post-Jihad, the design continued in production at Pandora 'Mech Works under Republic of the Sphere oversight, serving as a capable command vehicle for forces inheriting the Blakist industrial base on Terra.

The (A) configuration trades a portion of the Prime's infantry capacity for an alternate weapons arrangement suited to engagements against heavier opposition. It remains fully compatible with the standard R10 maintenance and logistics network, simplifying combined operations between configurations. The A variant is deployed by units expecting armored resistance and requiring greater direct fire capability alongside their troop delivery mission.

The (B) configuration offers a further tactical option within the R10 family, adapting the chassis for missions requiring different capabilities than the Prime or A. Like all R10 variants, the B benefits from the shared parts and logistics chain established for the platform. It is found in combined-arms formations where commanders require operational flexibility across varied mission profiles without sacrificing the core transport capabilities of the chassis.

The (Prime) configuration fulfills the infantry transport and fire support role the R10 was designed around. Its large bay accommodates a substantial complement of conventional infantry or battle armor, and the turret weapons allow the crew to engage enemy forces before, during, and after troop deployment. The Prime is the most widely distributed R10 configuration and sees service across garrison forces and planetary militias throughout the former Free Worlds League region and neighboring states. Commanders who restrict the Prime to a dedicated transport role often underutilize the design's active fire support potential.

The Interdictor variant was developed in 3087 to meet growing demand for electronic warfare capability at the vehicle level. Most of the machine gun ammunition supply is removed to free mass for a Guardian ECM Suite and additional armor plate. The Interdictor sacrifices most of the VV1's anti-infantry firepower in exchange for an electronic suppression bubble that degrades enemy targeting systems, disrupts C3 networks, and interferes with guided munitions in the lance's operating area. It is typically deployed in close support of more heavily armed vehicles, where it can extend its ECM coverage across the formation without being exposed to direct engagement. The Interdictor has found particular favor with forces expecting to face opponents relying heavily on advanced electronics.

This field modification emerged from technician feedback regarding the dual SlavTrack arrays' maintenance burden. Removing the arrays and replacing them with four standard Johnston Miniguns and four Johnston Light Machine Guns reduces the vehicle's upkeep demands considerably, at the cost of the arrays' linked-fire capability. Valiant Systems later formalized the conversion through their parts distribution network, supplying modification kits to units already operating the VV1. The variant remains officially designated VV1 to simplify logistics tracking, and is most common in units operating at extended distances from established depot support where the arrays' specialized maintenance requirements cannot be met reliably.

Introduced in 3082, the VV2 replaces the machine gun batteries entirely with eight Magshot Gauss rifles, nearly tripling the effective engagement range of the vehicle's primary armament. The trade-off is a significant reduction in volume of fire, making the VV2 less effective at close-range infantry suppression than the base model. The design has garnered more positive reviews among commanders who need a vehicle capable of engaging battle-armored infantry at distance, and the VV2 is frequently paired with one or two VV1s in urban defense lances. The VV1s manage close threats while the VV2 delivers ranged Gauss fire against harder targets, a combination that addresses the individual limitations of each model.

The VV22 represents an experimental Valiant Systems effort to address the VV2's vulnerability to multi-bearing threats. A second turret ring is added to accommodate a battery of standard small lasers, replacing the ER variants of the base design. The hull armor is upgraded to ferro-fibrous to compensate for the structural demands of the second turret. The result is a vehicle capable of engaging separate targets on different bearings simultaneously, an asset in complex urban engagements and fixed-installation defense. The dual-turret system carries substantial maintenance and cost penalties that have kept production numbers low. The VV22 is most commonly found in garrison assignments on worlds with the depot infrastructure to support it.

text.overview: The Red Kite Attack VTOL is a 25-ton combat rotary-wing aircraft introduced by Imstar Aerospace in 3093, designed to fill the reconnaissance and light attack needs of the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth. Imstar developed the design at its production facilities on Amity and Marik, capitalizing on a low acoustic profile to create a platform suited for operations in contested environments where stealth of approach is as important as firepower. Though the finished design carries significantly different armament than its original specifications called for, the Red Kite proved effective enough in service to earn a sustained production run. Against dedicated gunship platforms, it faces a persistent range disadvantage, but its exceptional speed allows it to dictate the terms of engagement, closing quickly with targets or disengaging before opponents can respond effectively.
text.capabilities:
The Red Kite mounts six Series 2CHM Medium Chemical Lasers, four in an oscillating turret and two in fixed forward mounts. These Clan-developed weapons were secured late in the development program, replacing an Imperator Napoleon Light AC/5 that had originally been specified for the turret. The chemical lasers generate no recoil, which initially appeared an ideal match for the oscillating turret mechanism.

However, the redesign introduced a significant flaw. The loading mechanism draws from a three-ton ammunition bay and cycles in synchronization with turret movement. If the turret has rotated more than sixty degrees off-center when the mechanism engages, the loader jams. Experienced crews learn to manage their engagement angles carefully to avoid triggering this limitation, making crew discipline as important to effective employment as raw firepower.

The fuel cell powerplant provides excellent performance for the airframe, pushing the Red Kite to a maximum speed of 183 kph. This makes it decisively faster than most dedicated gunship platforms, including the Yasha and Yellow Jacket. The trade-off is range. Chemical lasers are effective at close quarters but cannot match the standoff distance offered by the autocannons and missile racks carried by competing designs. The Red Kite must close with its targets to be effective, accepting exposure during the approach. Its ferro-fibrous armor provides reasonable protection for its weight class, but against prepared positions or sustained fire it remains vulnerable, as is typical of any VTOL platform.
text.deployment:
The Red Kite serves primarily in reconnaissance and screening roles across Marik-Stewart Commonwealth forces, later extending into Free Worlds League and Clan Wolf Empire inventories as political control over the production worlds changed. It is most commonly assigned to mixed combined-arms formations as a fast-reaction element, providing fire support and anti-infantry capability while using its speed advantage to avoid sustained engagement.

Units that field the Red Kite value its fuel cell powerplant for the logistical simplicity it provides in garrison and patrol roles, though extended operations far from maintenance support remain a limitation. In urban environments, the design's speed and low acoustic profile make it well-suited for rapid response missions. Commanders are advised to plan approach vectors that keep the oscillating turret within safe rotation angles throughout engagements, as managing the loader's jam vulnerability is the single most significant factor in effective employment of the design.
text.battleHistory:
The Red Kite entered service with the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth in 3093, developed by Imstar Aerospace at its production facilities on Amity and Marik. The design arose from Commonwealth commanders' recognition that their reconnaissance assets lacked a fast, quiet platform capable of operating near contested lines without drawing immediate attention. Imstar's experience producing aerospace fighters and conventional aircraft made them a logical choice for the program.

The original specification called for an Imperator Napoleon Light AC/5 as the primary weapon. During the later stages of development, Imstar secured access to Clan-developed Series 2CHM Medium Chemical Lasers, and the design was revised accordingly. The chemical lasers offered continuous fire without recoil, which appeared to simplify the turret design. The interaction between the oscillating mount and the loading mechanism proved more complicated in practice, producing the jam-prone behavior that has become the design's most persistent criticism in service.

Despite this limitation, the Red Kite's combination of speed and close-range firepower proved its value during the Clan Wolf and Lyran Commonwealth invasion of the former Free Worlds League in 3138. On Autumn Wind, a small Red Kite element escorted civilian VTOLs evacuating planetary leadership from Galveston City as Wolf forces broke through the defensive line. The intercepting Clan force included Dasher II OmniMechs captured from the Republic of the Sphere Armed Forces, machines capable of nearly matching the Red Kites' speed. The civilian VTOLs could not survive the micro laser fire that the Red Kites shrugged off, creating a difficult escort problem. When the mission commander's aircraft was downed in the opening exchange, surviving pilots executed a fighting withdrawal through the city's Two Rivers district. The pursuit ended when the pursuing Dasher IIs crossed the Panoply Bridge, which collapsed under their combined mass. All three OmniMechs survived the fifteen-meter plunge into the Felton River but were trapped for three hours, allowing the Red Kites and their civilian charges to escape.

Following the ilClan proclamation, production at Amity continued under Clan Wolf Empire control while the Marik facility remained within Free Worlds League territory, ensuring the design survived the political upheaval to serve multiple successor factions.

text.deployment: The standard Regulator serves as the backbone of Capellan hover cavalry formations, combining Gauss rifle firepower with exceptional mobility to fill the flanking and exploitation roles that CCAF tactical doctrine assigns to fast cavalry units. Every CCAF front-line regiment and most reserve formations deploy several lances, treating the vehicle as an essential force multiplier for their BattleMech elements. Its first combat action during Operation Guerrero in 3057 established the template that subsequent engagements would follow: Regulator lances flanking and destroying heavier opponents through superior positioning rather than direct firepower trades. Procurement demand has kept the Kingston plant at or near capacity since the vehicle entered service.

A single custom conversion examined by Maskirovka operatives on Poznan, this unique Regulator demonstrates the technical ingenuity of resourceful mercenary crews working with salvaged Word of Blake equipment. The vehicle's standard Gauss rifle was replaced with a Silver Bullet Gauss rifle apparently recovered from a former Blakist supply cache, and the ferro-fibrous armor was replaced with vehicular stealth armor incorporating an integral Guardian ECM suite. The conversion performed effectively in observed trials, easily outpacing its escorts and eliminating targets at range before opponents could effectively respond. The Maskirovka's documented interest in the configuration suggests the Confederation may seek to incorporate aspects of its design philosophy in future production models.

Created in 3064 to leverage the CCAF's expanding Arrow IV munitions arsenal, this variant removes the standard Gauss rifle and installs a Di Yu Huo Hellfire Arrow IV system. Engineers accepted a reduction in armor protection to accommodate the launcher and its fifteen rounds of ammunition, operating on the principle that the vehicle's speed would compensate for the thinner plating. The variant fills a dedicated indirect fire support role within Capellan combined-arms formations, providing hover-mobile artillery that can reposition rapidly between fire missions. Its primary limitation is the absence of direct-fire capability, making it entirely dependent on its mobility and escorting units for close defense.

This variant emerged from battlefield improvisation during the opening years of the Jihad, when Capellan technicians in the contested Capellan March began salvaging rotary autocannons and targeting computers from disabled Davion vehicles. Aldis Industries subsequently formalized the conversion process at their Betelgeuse facility. The RAC/5 paired with a linked targeting computer delivers exceptional close-range accuracy, earning a fearsome reputation among CCAF crews who prize the combination's effectiveness in pursuit operations. CASE protection for the ammunition bins reflects the lessons learned from early examples lost to internal explosions. The variant remains relatively uncommon, as the supply of Davion-sourced components constrains production volumes.

The base Regulator II serves as the premier medium hovertank in both the Republic Armed Forces and the Capellan Confederation's mechanized formations. Republic use concentrated heavily in the Principes Guard and the two other RAF brigades, where the dual-Gauss configuration supports the combined-arms tactics the newly formed Republic developed following the Jihad. Capellan deployment focused initially on planetary defense roles, where Aldis-Betelgeuse production supplemented vehicles transferred under the Lear agreement. The considerable cost premium over the original Regulator limits militia use, but both states treat the design as a front-line asset rather than a second-tier platform. Production from both Terra and Betelgeuse continues to supply active formations well into the ilClan era.
text.battleHistory:
The Regulator II's creation cannot be separated from the Word of Blake's strategic calculus during the Jihad. When Blakist forces occupied Terra and began directing civilian manufacturers, Aldis Industries found themselves working under an occupier with access to technical resources unprecedented in the Succession Wars era. The Blakists provided Aldis with complete Regulator documentation and directed them to develop an improved model, a directive the company fulfilled with the introduction of the Regulator II on Christmas Day 3076.

The deal brokered by David Lear following the Coalition's liberation of Terra proved decisive in shaping the design's spread. Lear negotiated the transfer of full Regulator II schematics to the Capellan Confederation as part of an agreement that also required the Republic of the Sphere to purchase surviving Regulator IIs from Coalition allies and resell half to the Confederation. The arrangement required significant political pressure, particularly because the Federated Suns was reluctant to surrender what had become a premium platform, but the final agreement is credited as one of the foundations of the Treaty of Tikonov.

Both manufacturing lines continued production into the Dark Age era. The Republic's Principes Guard maintained the highest percentage of Regulator IIs among the RAF brigades, though all three formations deployed the vehicles extensively. On the Capellan side, Aldis-Betelgeuse produced units primarily for planetary defense assignments, while front-line formations drew from both production lines depending on availability and political alignment. Diverging strategic priorities between the Republic and the Confederation eventually produced distinct variants, reflecting each state's differing doctrine and technology preferences while sharing the same capable basic chassis.

text.deployment: Developed at the Terra facility under Republic of the Sphere direction, this variant shifts the Regulator II from its long-range sniper role to a close-quarters combatant. The Inokuma Gauss rifle is replaced by a rotary autocannon mated to a Republic-licensed targeting computer, and a Guardian ECM suite is added to complicate the enemy's response. The design philosophy explicitly accepts the trade of reach for sustained close-range damage output, relying on the Regulator II's exceptional speed to close distance and the heavy ferro-fibrous armor to survive the approach. Republic forces found the configuration particularly effective for breakthrough operations and exploitation missions, where the RAC's rate of fire could overwhelm defenders before they could reorganize.

text.deployment: The flamer conversion transforms the Rhino into an anti-infantry and area-denial platform by replacing missile capacity with flamers. This modification primarily appeared during the Succession Wars, when conventional forces frequently faced hostile infantry in confined terrain. The conversion sacrifices the Rhino's long-range fire support role entirely in favor of close-range area effect capability, and units deploying the flamer variant typically operate alongside standard Rhinos to preserve the formation's standoff capability. The variant has seen periodic use into the modern era wherever enemy infantry tactics demand a dedicated incendiary response.

The Hagar is a unique experimental modification developed at the Leopard Armor facility on Terra in 2765. The conversion added a second turret and redistributed the vehicle's LRM racks between both turrets, creating two independently targetable missile batteries. An anti-missile system provided additional point defense capability. The project was declared obsolete in 2769 when political upheaval surrounding the fall of the Terran Hegemony forced termination before any meaningful production run. Only a handful of converted vehicles are known to have existed. The Hagar represents an innovative design direction that could have substantially improved the standard Rhino's tactical versatility under more stable circumstances.

The MG variant substitutes one LRM system for machine guns, equipping the Rhino to engage infantry that close with the vehicle. This conversion appeared shortly after the design's introduction and has remained popular with units operating in terrain where infantry contact is common, including urban and jungle environments. Standard industrial components make this modification feasible in most field workshops, and the variant has been documented in service from the Star League era through the ilClan period. The MG designation covers several closely related conversions that share the concept of trading long-range missile capacity for anti-infantry capability.

The ML variant removes missile systems in favor of medium lasers, eliminating ammunition dependence at the cost of long-range punch. This conversion appeared during the Jihad, when reliable resupply became difficult for many units and heat-efficient energy weapons offered a practical advantage in sustained operations. First Taurian Armored Lancer units are among the documented operators, mounting additional medium lasers in hull-facing positions to improve forward arc coverage. The variant has continued in use into the ilClan era as a cost-effective modification for formations operating far from established supply chains.

The Royal variant was issued exclusively to Star League Defense Force Royal units, pairing Artemis IV fire control on all three missile launchers with pulse laser upgrades, an anti-missile system, and a Guardian ECM suite. The XL engine conversion freed sufficient tonnage for these additions while keeping the vehicle within the standard Rhino's tactical framework. After the fall of the Star League, surviving Royal Rhinos became prized battlefield assets, their advanced components often stripped for use in other platforms when hulls were too damaged to repair. No Royal production has been documented outside the Star League period.

The SL variant replaces the LRM-10 with a short-range launcher, addressing the standard Rhino's poor performance against threats that close to short range. The conversion trades standoff firepower for a more balanced engagement envelope and proved popular with crews who frequently found themselves outmatched when enemies closed inside missile minimum range. Field workshops began producing this modification during the Star League period, and the variant has remained in service continuously ever since. The MUPL records an introduction date of 2840, though field use likely predates the formal documentation by over a century based on MegaMek source data placing the design's origin at 2724.

The standard Ripper operates across the Federated Suns and former Draconis Combine border regions, serving in general infantry delivery roles for line units and special operations formations alike. Cal-Boeing of Dorwinion's Belladonna facility remains the primary source for active procurement across multiple Successor States, with the Filtvelt line supplying the Filtvelt Coalition. The type is most effective when assigned to elite infantry, jump infantry, or scout units that can exploit its speed for rapid deployment and extraction.

The ER medium laser variant extends the Ripper's suppression range considerably, allowing pilots to clear a wider zone before troops touch down. This configuration is preferred by units operating in open terrain or wherever enemy infantry may attempt to engage from standoff distances the base medium lasers cannot effectively reach. First produced at Belladonna, the ERML variant entered service during the later stages of the Clan Invasion period and has remained in continuous production since.

Produced at the request of the Lyran Alliance Armed Forces, the Infantry variant is reconfigured to carry a full battle armor squad in place of conventional infantry. The XL engine provides the weight savings needed to accommodate the battle armor bay, but the trade-offs are significant: a single small pulse laser replaces the twin armament of other variants, and armor protection is reduced to one ton of heavy ferro-fibrous coverage. The type serves primarily within Lyran Alliance formations as a rapid battle armor insertion platform, most effective in scenarios where the squad's capabilities offset the vehicle's reduced defensive performance.

Produced at Draconis Combine request, this variant replaces the standard medium laser armament with a light PPC for extended-range capability and adds extra heavy ferro-fibrous armor plating, improving both reach and protection relative to the base model. The XL engine absorbs much of the weight cost. The variant serves throughout Draconis Combine reconnaissance and special operations formations, where the Ripper's speed combined with the light PPC's range suits the standoff suppression requirements common to deep insertion missions. Cal-Boeing of Dorwinion produces this variant at Belladonna for the Draconis Combine market.

The machine gun variant trades anti-vehicle effectiveness for improved performance against unarmored infantry concentrations, making it the preferred choice for garrison assignments and low-intensity operations. The twin machine guns are particularly effective during landing zone suppression against infantry without personal armor, allowing the crew to maintain a wider perimeter with reduced risk compared to the medium laser configuration in close-quarters urban work. Cal-Boeing of Dorwinion produces this variant at Belladonna for the Federated Suns market.

The small pulse laser variant offers improved accuracy at close range in exchange for reduced maximum range compared to both the base model and ERML configuration. This makes it well-suited to urban operations and dense terrain where engagements typically occur at very short distances. The variant is particularly favored by mercenary formations operating in contested urban zones, with Laws' Flight among the operator formations noted for effective employment of the type in close-terrain deployments.

production.manufacturer: Defiance Industries|General Motors|Alliance Defenders Limited|Benson and Bjorn

text.deployment: The standard Rommel served as the primary support companion to the Patton in Lyran and Federated Commonwealth armored formations, produced at both Hesperus II and Salem. Lyran production was active from the Late Succession Wars through the early Clan Invasion before shifting to the Gauss variant; Salem covered a similar early production window. The Outworlds Alliance independently fielded the standard Rommel through Alliance Defenders Limited at Alpheratz, where it remained in service under Outworlds Alliance and later Raven Alliance ownership through the Dark Age era.

The Rommel Gauss replaces the original autocannon with a Gauss rifle, extending effective engagement range and improving anti-armor lethality at distance. Defiance Industries produced it at Hesperus II through the Civil War era before phasing it out in favor of the Howitzer variant. General Motors' Salem facility proved the more committed producer, keeping the Gauss variant in continuous production from the Clan Invasion through the Dark Age, well past when Hesperus had discontinued it.

The production Rommel Howitzer entered service with the Lyran Guards from the Dark Age era, with the Fourteenth Lyran Guards being the first recipient. Produced by Defiance Industries at Hesperus II, it replaced the Gauss variant on that line and represents the Rommel's definitive evolved role as an artillery support vehicle. The Royal Guards and Arcturan Guards were next in the distribution queue. Its Long Tom cannon requires disciplined fire control to avoid friendly-fire incidents, a concern acknowledged within Lyran command staffs, and broader distribution or foreign sales remained uncertain at the time of its introduction.

The Rommel Howitzer Prototype was developed at the Defiance Manufacturing Annex at Kwangjong-ni beginning in 3077 as part of a vehicular modernization study. Six prototypes were produced and assigned to the factory defense reserve at Kwangjong-ni while production and logistical concerns were resolved. The Prototype uses an extralight engine, which proved too costly for series production and was replaced with a heavier standard engine in the production model. It saw no significant combat deployment outside the factory reserve role.

The Rommel Sealed is an amphibious and environmental protection variant intended for assault landings and hazardous-environment operations. It replaces the main gun with a heavy PPC backed by a Streak SRM launcher, and adds a short-range torpedo launcher for underwater engagement. Heavy ferro-fibrous armor and Guardian ECM complete the package. Produced at both Hesperus II and Salem from the Jihad era onward, it serves specialized formations tasked with planetary assault operations or fighting in contaminated environments.

The standard Rotunda saw its heaviest use with SLDF formations assigned to Periphery operations during the Star League era, deployed independently ahead of main forces to monitor enemy positions and relay communications intelligence. After the destruction of the Dieron facility in 2776, surviving original-specification vehicles distributed across a wide range of operators. ComStar maintained a modest fleet in reasonably complete condition through the Succession Wars, gradually replacing Buhallin components with equivalent Terran parts as original supply became critical. The Word of Blake later operated a portion of these. A smaller number persisted with independent mercenary commands and Periphery forces, valued for their endurance and low profile even as sourcing original components grew increasingly difficult.

The LRM variant arose when Pentagon Worlds technicians stripped fusion engines from Rotundas to support heavier combat systems during the early Succession Wars. Fitted with an internal combustion engine, two tons of standard armor, and a pair of LRM-5 launchers sharing a single-ton ammunition bin, this configuration preserved the Rotunda's wheeled mobility while extending its effective engagement range beyond the base model. It was documented primarily on the Pentagon Worlds in the years before Operation Klondike, where irregular and resistance forces relied on it for standoff harassment of heavier units. The combination of speed and long-range fire capability made this variant useful for engaging targets and withdrawing before a counterattack could be organized.

Of the three stripped variants, the RL configuration was the most focused on single-engagement firepower, carrying five fifteen-tube rocket launcher arrays in place of any sustained-fire weapons. Pentagon Worlds technicians favored it for ambush operations, where massed rocket fire could disable or destroy a heavier vehicle before the Rotunda withdrew. Its internal combustion engine and two tons of standard armor reflected the same component constraints as its sibling variants. The vehicle's light weight and wheeled mobility allowed access to terrain that heavier combat vehicles could not navigate, and its civilian silhouette provided cover until the moment of engagement. Once rockets were expended, however, the design had little tactical value remaining, and crews were expected to disengage immediately.

The SRM variant equipped a stripped Rotunda chassis with four SRM-2 launchers and a shared ton of ammunition, trading the LRM configuration's range for a higher rate of fire at close quarters. It was suited primarily to harassing infantry and lightly armored vehicles, where its volume of short-range fire compensated for the limited hitting power of individual SRM-2 racks. Like the other stripped variants, it appeared most frequently on the Pentagon Worlds before Operation Klondike, though the SRM configuration was occasionally documented across the broader Inner Sphere wherever technicians needed to return a stripped Rotunda chassis to service with whatever weapons were available locally.

text.overview:
The Sabaku Kaze Heavy Scout Hover Tank is a medium hover vehicle produced by Buda Imperial Vehicles on Dabih, entering service in 2695. Built as a redesign of the older Sand Devil hovercraft developed by Cairo Enterprises, the Sabaku Kaze, meaning "desert wind" in the Azami dialect, replaced the original petrochemical power plant with a fusion engine and upgraded both armor and weapons to military-grade standards. Conceived for the fast, mobile style of warfare favored by the Azami people of the Draconis Combine, the Sabaku Kaze was well-suited to hit-and-run operations and open-terrain patrol duties.

Cairo Enterprises retained ownership of the underlying design while Buda Imperial Vehicles held the exclusive production rights on Dabih, giving the tank a narrow production base that kept it largely an Azami-specific vehicle throughout its operational life.
text.capabilities:
The Sabaku Kaze carries a strong armaments package for a medium hover vehicle. Its primary weapons consist of four Intek Medium Lasers and two Intek Small Lasers, providing reliable anti-infantry and light vehicle firepower without ammunition dependence. Two Holly-4 SRM 4 launchers add burst-damage capability, and their placement allows the crew to engage threats from multiple directions during patrol. The Nissan 215 fusion engine pushes the Sabaku Kaze to a flank speed of 151 kilometers per hour, making it one of the faster medium designs of its era and well-suited to scouting and screening assignments.

Nimakachi Type 3 armor provides substantially greater protection than the Sand Devil carried, allowing the Sabaku Kaze to absorb hits that would have disabled its predecessor. The Dalban Series K communications suite and Dalban AQ targeting system support effective operations across the open desert terrain the design was built for.

The primary weakness is a logistics burden: the Sabaku Kaze uses components unique to the design, making field repair difficult without a dedicated supply chain. Its hover profile also limits effectiveness in rough or obstructed terrain where ground disruption would impede movement.
text.deployment: The Sabaku Kaze served exclusively within Azami forces during its production run, with only limited representation in the broader DCMS. Distribution outside Azami tribal units was minimal even at peak production. After the 2883 destruction of the Dabih factory, no new vehicles entered service. Surviving examples became increasingly difficult to sustain as proprietary replacement parts grew scarce, and most were cannibalized or taken out of frontline service by the late Succession Wars period. No meaningful numbers of Sabaku Kazes have been reported in active service since that time.
text.battleHistory:
The Sabaku Kaze's origins trace back to the Sand Devil, a scout hovercraft developed by Cairo Enterprises and introduced in 2452 among the Azami worlds of the Draconis Combine. The Sand Devil earned a strong reputation when the Combine moved to incorporate the Azami people in 2497. Azami tribal tank groups used their familiarity with desert terrain and the Sand Devil's speed to conduct raids and feints that frustrated Combine MechWarriors, and the vehicle's durability made it the foundation of Azami mobile warfare doctrine for generations.

The Sabaku Kaze entered the picture in 2673 when Buda Imperial Vehicles executives, touring Dieron District worlds, encountered the Sand Devil still in active service long after most vehicles of its age would have been retired. Impressed by the design's durability and the Azami's loyalty to it, Buda negotiated a permanent lease with the Dabih government and constructed a factory complex on the equatorial continent. The redesign retained the Sand Devil's flat-nose profile but incorporated a fusion power plant, military-grade armor, and a significantly heavier weapons suite. The new vehicle entered service in 2695 and quickly won acceptance among Azami warriors. A number of DCMS commanders adopted the type for combined-arms operations as well, though demand consistently outpaced Buda's production capacity.

The factory's end came in 2883 during a Davion raid on Dabih. Raiding forces targeted the factory's fission reactor containment structure, and the resulting fires spread radioactive debris across the facility and surrounding countryside, rendering the site uninhabitable for years. Buda Imperial Vehicles did not rebuild, and with no replacement production source, surviving Sabaku Kazes became increasingly difficult to maintain. The design used proprietary components, and as spare parts disappeared, units were cannibalized or pressed into experimental roles. Cairo Enterprises, which still holds the rights to the underlying design, has not licensed the type to any other manufacturer, and Buda has stated no plans to resume production.

text.deployment: The standard Saladin serves in harassment and shock roles across Draconis Combine armored formations, with the Azami worlds of the Dieron Military District providing ideal open terrain for its speed and firepower. The vehicle also appears in small numbers among mercenary commands and Free Worlds League cavalry regiments, where commanders use it as a heavy hit-and-run platform against enemy vehicles and light BattleMechs.

A widespread field modification appearing throughout the Succession Wars, the Armor variant removes one ton of autocannon ammunition to add armor protection where plate is available. Technicians perform this refit across the Inner Sphere, allowing units to field a more survivable Saladin at the cost of operational endurance.

Captured and converted Saladins appear in Clan logistical formations following the Clan Invasion, with the autocannon replaced by cargo equipment suited to rapid supply operations. This conversion exploits the Saladin's hover speed to move critical materials under fire, serving primarily in Clan rear-area logistics roles rather than front-line combat.

Produced at Scarborough Manufacturers' Al Na'ir facility during the FedCom Civil War, the LB-X variant replaces the original autocannon with an LB 20-X, allowing the crew to engage armored targets with solid slugs or scatter cluster munitions against aerospace assets and infantry. The upgrade saw service in Combine shock formations along the Federated Suns border.

A unique experimental conversion produced at the Trondel Refit and Repair Facility on Fronc during the Jihad, the Ifrit replaces the Saladin's ICE engine with a fusion plant, strips the autocannon in favor of a Particle Projection Cannon, and adds vehicular jump jets providing exceptional mobility. The design is a one-of-a-kind creation tied to Fronc Cuirassier operations and is not available for general issue.

The standard Saladin Mk II serves in Draconis Combine fast-strike and harassment roles, typically in lances of two or three vehicles supported by heavier armor. Its fusion engine and improved armor make it effective in sustained operations where the original Saladin would have required more frequent withdrawal. Both Al Na'ir and Algedi production support DCMS armored formations across the Combine's contested borders.

The BC3 variant integrates a boosted C³ computer system, linking the vehicle into networked lance formations and allowing the crew to share targeting data across BC3-equipped units. Produced at both Al Na'ir and Algedi, this configuration is assigned to advanced reconnaissance and fire-direction lances operating the Combine's C³ doctrine at tactical level.

Saracen units appear throughout the Inner Sphere in garrison and support roles, with the largest concentrations in Free Worlds League militia formations. The vehicle is most effective as a fire support platform operating behind friendly lines, leveraging its speed to reposition between LRM salvos. Mercenary commands frequently field mixed lances combining Saracens with Scimitars and Saladins to cover the full tactical range of the Scarborough hover family.

Produced at Scarborough's Al Na'ir facility during the FedCom Civil War, the MRM variant replaces the original LRM/SRM missile load with a multi-role launcher capable of engaging targets at variable ranges with greater raw firepower. The variant serves in Draconis Combine assault formations as a more aggressive fire support platform suited to offensive operations.

The Saracen Mk II operates as the fire support element in Combine fast-strike hover lances, typically paired with Saladin and Scimitar Mk IIs. Its multi-missile launcher and ER lasers provide a flexible long-to-medium range attack profile, and the fusion engine allows sustained operations without the fuel constraints that limited the original design.

The BC3 variant adds a boosted C³ computer, integrating the vehicle into networked lance formations for shared targeting across multiple units. Assigned to advanced combined-arms groups within the DCMS, this variant coordinates fire missions between hover lances and heavier supporting assets operating under the Combine's C³ doctrine.

The standard Savannah Master fills the cavalry and pursuit role across Inner Sphere militaries, fielded in platoons of four to six craft to coordinate high-speed attack runs. LCAF and AFFS commanders deploy it as a screening element, raid vehicle, and pursuit platform, using its speed advantage to exploit gaps in enemy formations before heavier forces can respond. The design performs well in open terrain where its velocity is decisive, and in urban environments where tight corridors limit the range advantage of heavier opponents.

Light mercenary commands adopted it widely as a cost-effective scout and harassment platform. Its low acquisition cost and minimal maintenance burden made it viable for commands that could not sustain heavier vehicles, and widely available spare components removed the logistical friction that plagued more specialized designs.

The Interdictor variant addresses the standard model's recognized vulnerability against enemy infantry. Introduced during the Jihad era, it replaces the standard laser with a weapons fit suited for area suppression, operating in fast-moving anti-infantry sweeps ahead of advancing conventional forces. Interdictor units clear approach routes and deny terrain to enemy foot soldiers, coordinating with infantry elements and other light vehicles in a combined arms role that the standard Savannah Master was never equipped to fill. The Lyran Alliance and later the Lyran Commonwealth deployed the variant extensively in defensive operations during post-Jihad reconstruction, particularly in contested urban zones where dispersed enemy infantry posed persistent threats to armored columns.

The Reflective variant emerged in the Republic era to address the proliferation of energy-weapon-equipped opponents across the Inner Sphere. Bowie Glinting Blade Reflective plating replaces the standard armor, substantially improving survivability against laser-armed forces at the cost of greater vulnerability to ballistic and missile weapons. The upgraded Defiance Model XII Extended-Range Medium Laser extends the craft's engagement range compared to the standard model, giving pilots more distance to maneuver before closing to effective range.

S.L. Lewis positioned the Reflective as a complement to the standard configuration rather than a replacement, mixing both types in combined formations where the standard model's lower cost and the Reflective's energy resistance create complementary tactical profiles.

The (SL) configuration was developed in 3033 as a field evaluation of an alternative weapons fit, replacing the standard Defiance B3M with a bank of light lasers intended to extend the craft's engagement envelope. Testing quickly revealed that the modifications strained the hovercraft's structural margins without producing a meaningful tactical improvement. The speed advantage that defined the Savannah Master's combat value was not sufficient compensation for the reduction in individual weapon effectiveness, and the LCAF concluded that the original configuration was superior across every relevant metric. The variant was discontinued after the evaluation period and never entered general service.

The base Saxon serves as a standard troop transport and convoy escort. It operates most effectively as part of combined arms formations, where its speed allows rapid infantry repositioning in response to developing threats. The single machine gun makes independent operations against armored opposition inadvisable, and commanders typically deploy it under the cover of heavier vehicles or BattleMechs. Its speed and capacity also make it useful for rapid evacuation and resupply missions behind the front line.

The (HQ) variant was introduced in 3074 by Defiance Industries as a mobile command and control platform for regimental and battalion commanders requiring both communications capability and the ability to remain mobile under fire. Three tons of communications equipment in the turret, paired with two extended-range medium lasers and a TAG system, allow the commander to direct artillery and aerospace strikes while retaining credible self-defense against lighter opponents. The Saxon's speed permits disengagement from threats exceeding its combat capacity.

The (Laser) variant is a field modification first appearing in 3071, replacing the standard Kicker-2 machine gun with an extended-range medium laser. The conversion eliminates the ammunition resupply burden and extends the vehicle's effective engagement range against light vehicles and infantry. It is common among experienced crews conducting extended operations where supply chain support is uncertain, and is distributed broadly across Lyran Alliance and Allied Coalition formations.

The (MASH) variant, produced by Quikscell Company beginning in 3071, converts most of the Saxon's interior into a mobile field hospital with two basic surgical operating theaters. The machine gun is retained for self-defense, with its magazine expanded to a full ton. The Saxon's speed and armor allow forward area medical support in conditions that would be untenable for conventional ambulance designs. Quikscell's variable production quality has led experienced recipients to verify surgical equipment operability before committing the vehicle to field operations.

The A Configuration converts the Scapha into a high-volume fire suppression platform. A single Rotary Autocannon 5, fed by three tons of ammunition, delivers devastating burst-fire capability against light vehicles and infantry concentrations. The vehicle sacrifices electronic warfare assets and scouting capability in exchange for sustained rate of fire, making this loadout effective in defensive engagements and convoy interdiction roles where volume of fire takes priority over precision or reconnaissance.

The B Configuration is a long-range precision strike platform built around a single Light Gauss Rifle with one ton of ammunition. The limited ammunition load means this configuration is not suited for prolonged engagements. Instead, the B relies on the Scapha's extreme speed to move into firing position, deliver accurate long-range shots against high-value targets, and disengage before the enemy can respond effectively. The configuration pairs well with reconnaissance assets that can identify and designate priority targets.

The C Configuration mounts an LB-10X Autocannon with two tons of ammunition, allowing the crew to select between standard armor-piercing slugs and cluster munitions. This flexibility makes the vehicle effective against conventional armor, where standard rounds punch through plating, and against infantry or lightly armored targets, where cluster fire inflicts broad-area damage. The C is valued by formations that regularly face mixed enemy compositions across varied engagement types.

The D Configuration is designed for close-range assault and fire coordination. A Snub-Nose PPC delivers hard-hitting direct fire at short range, while an iNarc Missile Launcher loaded with eight rounds marks targets for follow-on strikes from artillery or long-range missile units. The combination suits coordinated assault operations where multiple weapons systems need to engage the same targets in sequence, with the Scapha acting as both combatant and spotter.

The E Configuration transforms the Scapha into a highly mobile indirect fire support platform. A Thumper Artillery Cannon with three tons of ammunition provides area-suppression capability from a vehicle fast enough to reposition after firing before counter-battery fire arrives. The near-complete loss of direct combat capability means the E requires screening elements in most deployments. The configuration excels in fire support missions where speed and survivability after engagement outweigh the need for close-in defense.

The F Configuration serves as a medium-range fire support platform and artillery coordinator. An AC/5 guided by a Targeting Computer delivers accurate fire against armored targets, while two tons of mixed ammunition allow the crew to shift between round types as engagement conditions change. A Target Acquisition Gear unit enables the F to spot for artillery and semi-guided LRM systems, making it effective in combined-arms fire missions where coordination between multiple weapons platforms is required.

The G Configuration deploys the Scapha as a long-range precision platform integrated into a C3 fire coordination network. Two Light Autocannon 2s guided by a Targeting Computer provide accurate sustained fire at extended range, while a C3 slave unit links the vehicle into a shared targeting network. Two tons of mixed ammunition allow the crew to engage different target types. The C3 slave draws on network targeting data to improve accuracy against targets designated by other units in the network.

The H Configuration fields a pair of Medium Variable-Speed Pulse Lasers alongside a C3 slave unit, making it an effective intermediate-range combatant within an established network. Four additional heat sinks manage the thermal load generated by sustained pulse laser fire. The configuration benefits most from deployment in formations that already have C3 network infrastructure, providing reliable mid-range firepower with the accuracy advantages of shared targeting data from networked units.

The I Configuration is designed for command-and-control operations and target neutralization. A TSEMP Cannon serves as the vehicle's sole direct weapon, capable of shutting down enemy BattleMechs and combat vehicles through electromagnetic disruption. A C3 master computer coordinates the fire of networked units, making this configuration a high-value command asset. The I is best employed within a protective formation and directed toward capture or immobilization missions rather than front-line independent combat.

The J Configuration serves as a milestone in OmniVehicle development, being the first such vehicle to successfully integrate jump jets into its pod configuration. Seven jump jets allow the Scapha to bound over terrain obstacles that would stop conventional hover vehicles, dramatically expanding operational options in urban, broken, or heavily obstructed environments. A Guardian ECM Suite provides electronic denial capability, while three Medium Pulse Lasers in the turret deliver accurate close-range firepower. The J excels in city-fighting and assault roles where terrain masking and unexpected mobility are essential to survival.

The Primary Configuration deploys the Scapha as a fast reconnaissance and electronic warfare platform. An Angel ECM Suite and Bloodhound Active Probe provide comprehensive electronic detection and denial capability, while a supercharger pushes maximum speed past 220 km/h. The pair of turret-mounted Light PPCs, guided by a Targeting Computer, provide direct-fire capability beyond what most dedicated scouts carry. This configuration suits independent reconnaissance, advance screening, and disruption of enemy sensor networks while providing targeting data for follow-on strike units.

The standard Schildkröte entered service with the Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces in 3122, assigned primarily to planetary militias and garrison line units across the Commonwealth. Its combination of long-range autocannon fire, precision energy weaponry, and active missile defense made it well suited to static defensive positions and urban corridor operations. The tank’s heavy protection and motive system resilience allowed it to sustain fire from multiple attackers and remain operational, a capability valued by formations that lacked the depth to replace vehicles readily. Schildkrötes in standard configuration were widely distributed across lower-tier Lyran units, where their durability in defensive operations more than compensated for their limited ground speed.

Introduced in 3133, the HPPC variant replaces the standard autocannon and light energy weapon with a Heavy PPC and a two-tubed Short-Range Missile launcher supported by one ton of ammunition, along with additional heat sinks to manage the increased energy load. The trade-off shifts the Schildkröte’s engagement profile from longer-range combined-arms fire to a heavier close-range energy punch. The Heavy PPC delivers considerably more damage per shot against armored targets, though the reduced engagement envelope requires crews to position their vehicles more carefully. This variant was adopted by units expecting to operate in dense terrain, where the Heavy PPC’s raw hitting power outweighed the loss of stand-off engagement flexibility.

First produced in 3136, the Light Gauss variant replaces the base model’s LB 10-X Autocannon with a Light Gauss Rifle, extending the tank’s effective engagement range at the cost of some firing flexibility. The Light Gauss Rifle allows crews to engage targets before they close to effective return fire range, partially offsetting the Schildkröte’s well-documented mobility limitations. Heat output is reduced compared to the standard configuration, improving sustained fire endurance. This variant found particular favor in open terrain operations, where its longer reach allowed the slow-moving tank to engage advancing enemies before faster weapons could be brought effectively to bear.

The Plasma variant, introduced in 3138, replaces the LB 10-X Autocannon with a Plasma Rifle, adding a potent capability against both armored vehicles and infantry formations. The Plasma Rifle generates significant heat in targeted vehicles, degrading their combat efficiency even when it fails to cause outright destruction, and forcing BattleMech opponents into difficult heat management decisions during sustained exchanges. The variant imposes an additional heat burden on the Schildkröte’s own crew, requiring careful weapons management in extended engagements. Like all versions of the tank, its slow ground speed demands early positioning to ensure the Plasma Rifle’s engagement range can be effectively exploited.

The A Configuration trades long-range artillery for close-range missile saturation. Twin MRM-40 launchers in the forward pods deliver concentrated volleys against massed infantry or lightly armored vehicles, while a pair of MRM-10s join the turret-mounted lasers to engage targets from multiple angles simultaneously. One hundred missiles per full salvo can inflict serious damage on BattleMechs and is particularly effective at stripping the motive systems of opposing combat vehicles. This configuration sacrifices the standoff advantage of the Prime for a more aggressive close-support role, making it critical that supporting units shield the Schiltron from direct return fire.

The B Configuration emphasizes sustained indirect missile fire with improved guidance. Four LRM-15 launchers, each slaved to its own Artemis IV fire-control system, are divided between turret and front mounts. Eight tons of ammunition supports extended engagements. The direct-fire laser battery is reduced to one medium laser and two small lasers compared to the Prime, reflecting the heavier missile load. Artemis guidance improves cluster distribution and extends effective engagement range. The B Configuration is well suited for attrition warfare and siege-support roles, applying steady pressure to fortified positions while remaining at standoff distances from defensive fires.

The C Configuration was designed for operations where resupply cannot be guaranteed. All weapon pods carry large lasers in a turret mount, eliminating ammunition dependency entirely. The sustained energy output is substantial at medium range, though the absence of ammunition-based weapons limits versatility across engagement distances. This configuration performs best during extended campaigns in supply-constrained theaters or when operating from mobile fire bases where logistics support is uncertain. It sacrifices flexibility for operational independence, and its effectiveness drops sharply against targets at long range.

Introduced in 3063, the D Configuration incorporates weapons technology drawn from Federated Suns programs. A pair of rotary autocannon/5s occupy the turret, slaved to a targeting computer for precision engagement of fast-moving targets. Six tons of autocannon ammunition ensures sustained fire across extended engagements. An LRM-15 mated to an Artemis IV fire-control system supplements the autocannons at longer range. This configuration lacks direct-energy backup weapons but compensates with exceptional rate of fire and guided missile support at range. It is considered the most versatile of the Schiltron family for combined-arms operations against mixed BattleMech and vehicle formations.

Introduced during the Jihad, the E Configuration was developed to address the fragmented supply environment of that conflict. Three MML-9 launchers occupy forward-facing pods with three tons of combined LRM and SRM munitions. The turret carries three light autocannon/5s with two tons of ammunition, providing a sustained direct-fire capability at medium range. The ability to fire either LRM or SRM munitions from the same launchers makes this configuration valuable when resupply sources are unreliable, as crews can adapt to whatever compatible ammunition is available in the field. The mixed launcher and autocannon loadout covers most engagement ranges the Schiltron is likely to encounter.

The Primary Configuration mounts a pair of Arrow IV artillery systems in forward-facing pods, supported by eight tons of mixed munitions including homing rounds. Two medium lasers and four small lasers in a turret mount provide minimal close-defense capability. All configurations retain the base chassis C3 master computer and Guardian ECM suite. This configuration is intended to operate well behind the front line, using homing artillery rounds designated by forward C3 network members to engage targets far outside visual range. It is the most purely indirect-fire of the Schiltron's configurations and is entirely dependent on friendly screening forces for protection against direct assault.

As a field conversion rather than a planned design, the Schrek AC Carrier has no fixed production standard. Most examples retain the basic hull layout of the original Schrek, with ICE powerplants and autocannon batteries substituted for the original fusion engine and PPCs. These vehicles circulate primarily in garrison and militia roles where lower operational costs outweigh diminished firepower. Configuration and components varied widely based on available materials and local technical expertise.

Produced by the Alphard Trading Corporation on Leximon for the Lothian League beginning around 3140, this variant formalizes the autocannon conversion concept with three Marian-sourced Ultra AC/10s backed by six tons of ammunition. Ferro-fibrous armor improves survivability compared to typical field conversions. An ICE powerplant keeps production and maintenance costs accessible for Lothian League logistics, and the design represents the League's investment in a domestically producible anti-armor platform.

text.overview:
The Schrek Gauss Carrier stands as a fundamental reimagining of the Schrek chassis for Capellan operational priorities in the Dark Age. Developed in cooperation between the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces and Grumman Amalgamated at its Shiro III facility in the Duchy of Andurien, the design emerged from the lessons of the Victoria War, which demonstrated the importance of stealth and precision in anti-armor operations against sophisticated opposing forces.

Rather than the direct-fire intimidation of its ancestor, the Gauss Carrier emphasizes covert engagement, using stealth armor and electronic countermeasures to approach undetected before delivering precise long-range rifle fire. Produced primarily for CCAF and Duchy of Andurien forces, the design has seen deployment along the Capellan/Davion border and in contested Andurien frontier zones.
text.capabilities:
The Gauss Carrier's three Light Gauss Rifles deliver consistent, accurate fire at ranges comparable to the original Schrek's PPCs, without the electromagnetic signature that makes PPC-armed vehicles conspicuous to enemy sensors. The combination of stealth armor and an integrated ECM suite allows the vehicle to approach engagement positions with substantially lower detection risk than comparable heavy armor. A Light engine reduces mass requirements, enabling the armor and sensor suite that define the variant's tactical role. Four tons of ammunition provide a reasonable sustained engagement capacity.

Tactical limitations are significant, however. Light Gauss Rifles lack the raw damage output of the Schrek's original PPC armament, and the ammunition supply is a finite engagement capacity that limits extended operations. The stealth armor's signature suppression requires active energy, and the Light engine restricts top speed. The design demands careful tactical placement, relying on concealment and first-strike precision rather than the sustained fire suppression that characterized earlier Schrek variants.
text.deployment: Produced by Grumman Amalgamated on Shiro III in the Duchy of Andurien and by Aldis Industries on Betelgeuse for the Capellan Confederation, the Gauss Carrier serves primarily with CCAF and Duchy of Andurien armor formations in the Dark Age and ilClan eras. Its stealth capability and precision armament suit it to reconnaissance-in-force and screening roles alongside heavier Capellan assets, particularly in contested border regions where unexpected engagement ranges can disrupt an opponent's tactical planning.
text.battleHistory:
The Victoria War of the early Dark Age exposed persistent vulnerabilities in Capellan conventional armor doctrine, particularly the difficulty of engaging technically superior Federated Suns forces in open terrain where heavier firepower and better-armored vehicles held decisive advantages. CCAF planners and Grumman Amalgamated's design teams on Shiro III collaborated on a response that prioritized stealth and precision over the raw bombardment capacity of earlier Schrek variants.

The resulting Gauss Carrier entered production around 3119, representing Grumman's synthesis of stealth technology lessons from the Victoria conflict with the familiar Schrek hull that CCAF logistics networks already supported. Deployment concentrated initially on the Capellan/Davion border, where the vehicle's ability to conduct covert fire missions complemented existing combined-arms formations. The Duchy of Andurien, maintaining a separate production line at Betelgeuse through Aldis Industries, has deployed the type in smaller numbers against Free Worlds League forces along contested border regions, though the Duchy's access to Aldis facilities remains a point of ongoing logistical complexity.

production.manufacturer: Aldis Industries|Aldis Industries|Alphard Trading Corporation|New Samarkand Metals

text.deployment: Typically deployed in supporting fire roles behind heavier armor formations, the standard Schrek excels when positioned in prepared emplacements or hull-down behind terrain. The configuration operates best in open terrain where its long engagement ranges can be exploited and enemy counterfire minimized. Found in armor-heavy formations across the Inner Sphere from the early Succession Wars through the ilClan era, most commonly paired with Demolisher heavy tanks or similar close-range assets.

A field modification first documented in 2833, this variant drops a modest amount of armor to mount small anti-infantry weapons, typically a machine gun or small laser. Units operating in environments with significant infantry threat devised this conversion to address the base Schrek's complete vulnerability to infantry attack. As a field refit with no fixed production standard, configuration and specific components varied considerably between units.

Developed during the Jihad and produced by New Samarkand Metals, this variant trades one full-power PPC for a light PPC and integrates a C3 master computer, Guardian ECM suite, and anti-missile system. Designed to serve as a command and coordination vehicle for C3-equipped armor lances, the (C3M) variant sacrifices some raw firepower to provide substantial command and defensive value within organized combined-arms formations. Found primarily in Draconis Combine service.

components.armor: New Samarkand Metals New Samarkand Teppeki Hardened

text.deployment: Developed by New Samarkand Metals and inspired by the Narukami heavy tank, this variant replaces two PPCs with a pair of LB 10-X autocannons, creating a versatile anti-tank and anti-air platform. Hardened armor greatly improves survivability against the cluster munitions and precision fire the design was built to withstand, while CASE-protected ammunition bins reduce the risk of catastrophic explosions. Produced from 3120 onward at New Samarkand.

Produced at Aldis facilities on Betelgeuse and Terra and at New Samarkand Metals' plant beginning around 3058, this modernized variant replaces the original GoreTex engine with a Hermes 240 XL, freeing mass for seven additional tons of heavy ferro-fibrous armor and a speed increase to 64 kph. The XL variant addresses the base Schrek's most criticized shortcomings, improving both protection and mobility while retaining the full three-PPC armament. Active from the Civil War era through the ilClan period.

The standard Scimitar serves in mixed hover lances across the Inner Sphere, most commonly alongside Saracens in combined-arms formations. The vehicle's direct-fire capability complements the Saracen's missile systems, and together the two types cover a broad tactical range. DCMS formations in the Dieron Military District were among the largest sustained operators, fielding the Scimitar in combined hover lances through the Clan Invasion period.

Working from the TAG variant, Combine technicians replaced all weapons with a rotary autocannon and C³ computer, thickening the armor using heavy ferro-fibrous plate. Introduced during the Jihad, the C3 Scimitar functions as a networked reconnaissance platform capable of sharing targeting data across a lance while defending itself with the rotary cannon. It serves in Jihad-era and later Combine combined-arms formations as a fire-direction node.

A field modification replacing the autocannon and SRM 2 racks with additional missile launchers, the Missile variant sacrifices direct-fire punch for greater standoff range and ammunition variety. Technicians throughout the Inner Sphere have produced this conversion wherever missile components are more readily available than autocannon ammunition, making it one of the more common Scimitar field refits.

Produced at Scarborough's Al Na'ir facility during the Clan Invasion, the TAG variant strips secondary weapons and installs a targeting acquisition gear system to support Arrow IV artillery strikes. Combine forces used TAG Scimitars extensively as forward observer platforms in counter-Clan operations, pairing their hover speed with the ability to designate targets for indirect fire assets operating beyond visual range.

The standard Scimitar Mk II serves in harassment and direct-fire support roles across Combine armored formations, operating in mixed hover lances with Saladin and Saracen Mk IIs. Its short-to-medium range weapons load makes it most effective in close terrain where enemy formations can be ambushed and harassed at short range. Both Al Na'ir and Algedi production lines supply the DCMS, with the Algedi facility becoming the primary source of the base configuration after 3135.

The 3136 Upgrade replaced several weapons systems and fire control components with more capable equipment, substantially improving effectiveness against modern opponents. Produced at the Al Na'ir facility, this variant serves in front-line Combine cavalry regiments during the Dark Age period and represents the most capable version of the Scimitar line outside the BC3 network configuration.

The BC3 variant adds a boosted C³ computer to the standard Mk II weapons load, integrating the vehicle into networked lance formations and enabling coordinated fire across multiple units. Produced at Al Na'ir, this version is assigned to advanced combined-arms formations operating the Combine's C³ doctrine, typically alongside the BC3 variants of the Saladin and Saracen Mk IIs.

text.deployment: Planetary militias, mercenary commands, and bandit organizations across the Inner Sphere employ the Scorpion as a garrison and security platform, typically deploying it in company and battalion strength to compensate for its individual limitations. Standard doctrine pairs Scorpion formations with faster screening elements to protect flanks and suppress opponents before they can close to ranges where the autocannon's tracking weaknesses become critical. The vehicle performs most reliably in defensive positions where terrain directs opponents along predictable approach routes.

The Armor variant addressed the Scorpion's most significant tactical liability by adding ferro-fibrous protection during the Clan Invasion era, increasing survivability in sustained garrison engagements without altering the vehicle's role. Federated Commonwealth forces at Layover and Draconis Combine units at Luthien adopted this version as an incremental improvement requiring no modifications to the existing hull. The enhanced protection made the vehicle more durable against weapons common to Clan equipment, and the variant gradually displaced older models in militia inventories where factory access permitted replacement.

The Hardened variant applies reinforced armor to the Scorpion hull at a significant cost in ground speed, producing an exceptionally durable light vehicle suited to fixed defensive positions. Aldis Industries developed this version on Betelgeuse during the Dark Age for Capellan Confederation garrison assignments where survivability in prepared fortifications mattered more than mobility. The reduced speed renders this variant unsuitable for mobile operations, but in chokepoint defense and fortified lines it absorbs punishment that would quickly destroy standard Scorpions. Production continued from the Late Republic era through the ilClan period.
